title: Electric potential & potential energy
examples: What is the difference between electric potential and electric potential energy?
How does the distance between charges affect the potential?
Can you give an example of equipotential lines in real life?

explain.say: Today we learn about electric potential and potential energy. We will see how these concepts relate to charges.
The electric potential V at a point depends on the charge and distance. The formula is V equals k times q divided by r.
Equipotential surfaces are places where the electric potential is the same. Charges on these surfaces do not work to move.
When moving a charge, the work done is related to the change in potential. Work equals the charge times the potential difference.
Consider moving a small positive charge between two points. The work done is calculated using the potential difference.
In a real life example, a battery provides a potential difference. This difference does work to move a charge through a circuit.

faq.q: What is the difference between potential and potential energy?
faq.a: Potential energy is the stored energy in a system due to position. Potential is the energy per unit charge. One is energy, the other is energy per charge.
asks: How are PE and V related?
Is potential energy measured in Joules or Volts?

faq.q: Do electric field lines always cross equipotential lines?
faq.a: Yes, electric field lines are always perpendicular to equipotential surfaces. This means they cross at right angles.
asks: What is the relationship between E and V?
Why must the lines cross at ninety degrees?

faq.q: If I move a positive charge against the field, do I do positive work?
faq.a: Yes, if you move a positive charge against the electric field, you must do positive work. This increases the potential energy.
asks: Does the work done depend on the path taken?

faq.q: Does the work done depend on the path taken between two points?
faq.a: No, the work done moving a charge between two points depends only on the start and end potentials. This is a conservative field.
asks: Does the path matter for work done?

faq.q: What is the unit for electric potential?
faq.a: The unit for electric potential is the volt. One volt is one joule per coulomb.
asks: What is the unit for voltage?
How many Joules per Coulomb is one Volt?

facts: Electric potential V is defined as the potential energy per unit charge.
The electric potential due to a point charge follows the inverse square law, similar to gravity.
Equipotential surfaces are always perpendicular to the electric field lines.
The work done moving a charge is equal to the charge multiplied by the potential difference.

quiz.say: A charge moves from a point of potential V1 to a point of potential V2. The work done is:

options.show: k q / r2 - k q / r1
options.say: k q / r2 - k q / r1

options.show: k q / r2 + k q / r1
options.say: k q / r2 + k q / r1

quiz.why: Work done depends only on the initial and final potentials, not the path taken.

wrong.0: Work is only zero if the potential difference is zero, which is not guaranteed.
wrong.2: This formula incorrectly assumes work depends only on the initial and final positions, ignoring the charge q.
wrong.3: Adding the potentials incorrectly calculates the total work done.

quiz.say: Which statement correctly describes equipotential lines?

options.show: Only charges on equipotentials have zero potential.
options.say: Only charges on equipotentials have zero potential.

options.show: Field lines cross equipotentials at right angles.
options.say: Field lines cross equipotentials at right angles.

options.show: Field lines are parallel to equipotentials.
options.say: Field lines are parallel to equipotentials.

quiz.why: The perpendicular relationship is a fundamental property linking the electric field and potential.

wrong.0: Zero potential only occurs at specific points, not everywhere on the surface.
wrong.2: If they were parallel, the potential would not change across the field line.
wrong.3: They can be any shape depending on the charge distribution.

quiz.say: If you move a positive charge against the direction of the electric force, the work done is:
quiz.why: Doing work against a field increases the potential energy, requiring positive work.

wrong.0: Work is only zero if the charge moves along an equipotential surface.
wrong.1: Electric potential energy is a property of position, not speed.
wrong.3: Negative work implies the electric field did the work on the charge.
